creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`tai install --dry-run` reports skill directories differently from the install it is previewing. Two symptoms, one cause: both the checksum recompute and the frontmatter parse sit behind the same `if !opts.DryRun` guard in `installFileAsset`.

- Every skill directory counts as `updated`, where a real install of the same profile counts it `unchanged`. A directory's checksum is computed twice: once from the source when the asset is resolved, then again from the installed copy once includes are resolved and the adapter has rewritten the frontmatter. The manifest holds the second. Dry-run only ever computes the first, so it compares source against installed and never matches.
- The dropped-frontmatter warnings added by `native` (af96f6f) never print for skills. A skill's SKILL.md is parsed while its directory is copied, so `resolved.Warnings` is still empty when dry-run collects it. Personas and delegates are single files and do warn.

The impact is that dry-run cannot be used for what it exists for. Someone checking an install before letting it run sees every skill listed as `updated`, which says nothing about which ones actually changed, and sees no warnings, which reads as confirmation that their frontmatter survived.

Parsing the source SKILL.md instead of the installed copy is not a fix on its own: when an include replaces the file, the source reports fields the installed copy will not have.

Found 2026-08-16 while integrating the `restored` counting and `native` frontmatter work. Pre-existing, and neither of those caused it. Both slots hit it independently, from opposite directions.
title: install --dry-run misreports skill directories: always updated, and no frontmatter warnings
